newsitem.title: POLAND: Only BIG in bid for Gdanski.
newsitem.headline: Only BIG in bid for Gdanski.

text.p: Bank Inicjatyw Gospodarczych SA (BIG) placed the only bid for the Polish treasury's 31.9 percent stake Bank Gdanski SA before the January 6 deadline, a senior finance ministry official said on Tuesday.
"There is only the BIG bid, there are no more offers," Wieslaw Federowicz, the head of the ministry's banking department, told Reuters.

On Monday BIG, which together with its subsidiaries already controls about 31 percent of Gdanski, and has long signalled its interest in gaining a strategic stake, confirmed it had submitted a bid for Gdanski stake but it was not clear whether there were any other bidders.
Federowicz said a special ministry committee began studying the offer and should be ready with its recommendation for the finance minister by the end of this month.
If the minister accepts the recommendation the ministry would start negotiating the sale, Federowicz said.

The ministry announced its offer to sell its 31.9 percent stake left after Gdanski's flotation in December 1995, on December 16. The ministry as the representative of the state treasury currently holds about 37 percent of shares but five percent of shares are set aside as a special reserve.
The Bank of New York as a depositary bank currently holds 19.5 percent of Gdanski's shares, represented by 19.5 percent of the bank's GDRs held by foreign investors.
